title: When the Recipe Wakes
premise: Odile Nystrom has spent five years running 'Hollowpoint,' an anonymous account that leaks what the Marrow Creek school board buries — until his best friend Theo vanishes, leaving behind a ring of keys and a half-deleted folder of evidence. Following the keys, Odile uncovers that the board covered up a toxic mold scandal in the old wing, and that Theo found out the hard way. As prom approaches and the board's fixer closes in, Odile must choose between staying safe behind anonymity and going public as himself. In the end he livestreams the buried records during prom night, the board collapses under public fury, and Theo is found alive — but Odile learns justice won outside the law costs him the careful, hidden life he built.
about_author: S. M. Vasquez is a former high school debate coach who writes stories about teenagers who refuse to wait for permission. They live in the Pacific Northwest with two cats named after whistleblowers.

chapters.title: Five Years of Careful
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. We meet him mid-post on Hollowpoint, redacting every traceable habit from his writing, while his best friend Theo teases him about being paranoid. The emotional beat is the quiet ache of a life lived small — safety purchased at the price of being known.

chapters.title: The Keys on the Windowsill
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Theo misses their weekly diner ritual; at his apartment Odile finds a ring of unlabeled keys and a laptop wiped except for one encrypted folder named 'prom.' Fear arrives cold and specific. Beat: dread replacing irritation.

chapters.title: What Anonymous Knows
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. He combs Hollowpoint's archives and realizes Theo had been quietly feeding him tips for months — including one about the condemned east wing. His anonymous source was his best friend all along. Beat: vertigo of betrayal and love entangled.

chapters.title: Key One: The Custodian's Closet
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, first key. The keys open a maintenance closet holding boxes of maintenance complaints about black mold, dated years back, stamped 'resolved' by someone who never inspected. Beat: first proof the rot is literal and institutional.

chapters.title: People Who Smile Too Easily
chapters.summary: Alternating POV introducing Board President Dana Voss and her fixer, Mr. Aldous Reeve, who notices someone accessed district storage. Their chapters are polished menace — power as hospitality. Beat: the reader meets the antagonist smiling.

chapters.title: Key Two: Room 114
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A classroom key leads to sealed-off Room 114 where air tests were faked; he finds Theo's handwriting on a sticky note: 'they knew before the renovation.' Someone else has been in the room recently. Beat: he's not alone in this hunt.

chapters.title: Found Family, Fraying Edges
chapters.summary: Odile's POV with friends Priya and Marcus, who notice his unraveling. He can't explain without exposing Hollowpoint. Priya guesses anyway and doesn't flinch. Beat: warmth — the first time being seen feels like relief instead of risk.

chapters.title: The Fixer's Visit
chapters.summary: Reeve's POV then Odile's. Reeve interviews students about 'vandalism' in the east wing, lingering on Odile a beat too long. That night Odile finds his dorm door unlocked though he locked it. Beat: paranoia becomes physical, the walls closing in.

chapters.title: Key Three: The Records Annex
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The third key opens a district annex where he photographs settlement agreements paid to sick staff, hush money routed through a booster club. His hands shake — this is bigger than mold. Beat: awe and terror at the scale.

chapters.title: What Theo Was Building
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. She and Marcus decode Theo's encrypted folder using his old passphrase — a joke only the four of them share. Inside: a timeline meant for publication, addressed 'for O., when you stop hiding.' Beat: grief sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: An Offer, Gently Made
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. She summons Odile with a scholarship-shaped bribe and a motherly warning about 'troubled boys who chase conspiracies.' He smiles and lies well. Beat: corruption wearing kindness; Odile passes his first test of nerve.

chapters.title: Burned
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Hollowpoint's server is seized via a warrant aimed at 'a person unknown'; his five years of anonymity evaporate in a single afternoon. Reeve leaves a business card in his mailbox. Beat: the safe life ends; no more hiding.

chapters.title: The Whistleblower Who Cried Wolf
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. School turns on Odile as rumors paint him unstable; even teachers distance themselves. Priya refuses to leave his side. Beat: isolation — the cost of truth-telling without allies or law on your side.

chapters.title: Key Four: The Boathouse
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The fourth key opens a boathouse where he finds signs Theo hid here — food wrappers, a sleeping bag, a note: 'If I go quiet, it wasn't my choice.' Hope reignites: Theo may be alive and hunted. Beat: desperate hope.

chapters.title: Prom Is a Deadline
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Voss plans a triumphant prom-night ribbon-cutting for the renovated wing; Odile realizes the ceremony is both her shield and his window — every camera, every parent, in one gymnasium. Beat: the plan crystallizes into audacity.

chapters.title: Recruiting the Yearbook
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The trio recruits yearbook staff, AV kids, and a disillusioned teacher's aide — a ragtag crew with cameras, drones, and grudges. Beat: found family assembling into something like an army.

chapters.title: Key Five: What the Basement Kept
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The final key opens a basement archive: original air-quality reports, and a voicemail log proving Voss ordered retesting suppressed. Also, fresh footprints. Reeve knows he's coming. Beat: triumph shadowed by trap.

chapters.title: Taken
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Reeve corners him; Odile barely escapes with the drive, learning Reeve detained Theo 'for his own protection' weeks ago. Rage replaces fear entirely. Beat: the point of no return — he will burn his caution down.

chapters.title: Prom Night
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. Under disco lights and a ribbon-cutting speech, the crew hijacks the AV feed: documents, photos, Theo's timeline, broadcast to every phone in the gym. Voss's smile dies on the jumbotron. Beat: climax — spectacle as justice.

chapters.title: Where They Kept Him
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Acting on a detail from Theo's notes, police — now unable to look away — find Theo held at a district-owned property under a falsified psychiatric hold. Odile identifies himself by name, on record, for the first time in five years. Beat: courage completing its arc.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Loudly
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Reunion in a hospital hallway; hearings begin; Voss resigns mid-session and Reeve takes the fall she hands him. Odile posts one final Hollowpoint entry signed with his real name, then retires the account. Beat: bittersweet vindication.

chapters.title: When the Recipe Wakes
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, epilogue. Summer: the east wing is gutted and remediated, the four friends eat at their diner booth, and Theo asks what Odile will build next. He answers: something open-source, something with his name on it. Beat: peace earned, identity reclaimed.
